critique: The centered title panel and coral Start button produce an immediate title-to-action hierarchy, but the panel consumes much of the upper play field and makes the actual slope preview feel secondary and compressed. The skier is very small relative to the panel, while trees and flags have similar visual weight, so the playable subject is not the obvious next thing the eye discovers. The instruction line inside the panel and the top HUD are legible only at close inspection, weakening the transition from starting the game to understanding control.
suggestion: Reduce the title panel's height and lift it slightly to reveal more of the slope while preserving the title as the first read. Increase the skier and its trail enough to become the clear secondary focal point, then use flags and trees as a directional corridor toward it rather than equally weighted objects. Enlarge and simplify the control instruction beneath Start, maintaining a strong title → Start → skier → controls sequence; retain the HUD as a quiet tertiary status band.
